data.body:
MERGED — Gerrit 1317 (`34cd: defer autodeploy while a review runs`), on main.

THE ROOT CAUSE IS SHARPER THAN THIS TICKET ORIGINALLY STATED, and the correction matters. The bot ALREADY
drains — but only half of it:
    app.py:117              await asyncio.wait_for(queue.join(), timeout=shutdown_drain_seconds())
    docker-compose.yml:112  stop_grace_period: 1320s
so a WEBHOOK-QUEUED review is protected today. But reconcile.py:223 awaits `voter.review_and_vote` INLINE,
outside that queue: with an empty queue, `queue.join()` returns immediately and `reconcile_loop` is
cancelled within SHUTDOWN_CANCEL_SECONDS (~10s).
THE RECONCILER IS THE RETRY PATH — so the SELF-HEAL mechanism is precisely the unprotected one. That is the
live-lock, and it corrects my earlier framing that this "self-heals benignly": the retry is what dies.

OPTION CHOSEN: DEFER. DRAIN was rejected because sleeping until idle holds the deploy flock for the whole
wait, blocking the obs/certbot re-materializers. COALESCE was rejected as insufficient alone — a debounce
reduces seven deploys to fewer, but one deploy still kills a review, so it cannot satisfy AC1 — and DEFER
subsumes its benefit for free, since TARGET is recomputed each tick so deferred ticks collapse into one
deploy at the newest tip.

DEVIATION FROM THE PLAN, flagged: the plan grouped DEFER as needing "no new bot surface". It does need a
busy signal. Implemented as the minimum — an `in_flight` field on the EXISTING /health route (no new
endpoint, `status` unchanged), counted around `review_and_vote`, which is the single funnel for BOTH the
worker and the reconciler.
BOUND: DEPLOY_DEFER_MAX=1800s, justified against the app's own REVIEW_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=1200 which no single
review can outlive, so the bound is only reachable by a chronically busy bot.
A SUBTLETY WORTH KEEPING: keying the bound to the target SHA (as BACKOFF_FILE does) would DEFEAT it —
during a burst TARGET advances almost every tick, resetting the timer forever. It is keyed to the deferral
EPISODE, cleared on deploy/idle/up-to-date.

AC4 OBSERVABILITY: two countable tokens, deliberately NOT folded into AUTODEPLOY_ERROR so a routine
deferral does not page — AUTODEPLOY_DEFERRED -> deploy_deferrals, and AUTODEPLOY_REVIEW_INTERRUPT ->
review_interrupts with a new paging alarm rebar-autodeploy-review-interrupts. The drain fails OPEN on an
unreadable signal (a bot that cannot answer /health is likely broken and deploying is the fix) but that case
is COUNTED — a silently broken probe would otherwise restore the original blindness. A payload missing
in_flight counts as unknown, never idle.

RED: reverting autodeploy.sh to HEAD gave 10 of 13 failures; the 3 that still pass assert already-correct
behaviour (idle deploys, unreachable bot still deployable). Burst case (AC5): six ticks with the tip
advancing while one review runs -> zero recreations, then exactly ONE compose-build at the newest tip.

RESIDUAL GAP FILED: 9ec0-02b2-8494-4ea5 (wormy-camlet-puma), linked discovered_from this ticket. This fix is
DEPLOY-SIDE and mitigates but does not close the shutdown-side half: any manual restart, host reboot, or
autodeploy's own rollback still kills a reconciler review.
